items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge Upsell (year 1.5 "is it worth it" math)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates, 100 members (13-24 months post-install, not on Concierge). Note: dedupe needed. Albert Romano appears twice; treat as one contact.
**Why this one:** Largest qualified, high-intent list (100). These people already survived year 1, trusted us through their first annual service, and have real revenue attached. This is warm, permission-based, and clears the 12-month floor.
**Subject line (primary):**
`The year 1.5 question we get asked most`
**Alternates:**
1. (curiosity) `Is the Concierge thing actually worth it?`
2. (specific) `Here is the $99 math, no spin`
3. (authority) `What we cover so you never think about it`
4. (pain) `Filter swaps, parts, priority line. Handled.`
**Preview text:**
`The honest math on whether Concierge makes sense for your home. No pressure either way.`
**Body:**
Hi Albert,
It has been about 17 months since we installed your water system, which means you have already been through your first annual service with us. So here is the question we get asked most right around now: "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
Fair question. Here is the honest math.
Concierge is $99/mo. It covers your annual service, filter swaps, priority phone support, and parts coverage on your standard install components. If you are currently handling service pay-as-you-go, add up what a year of swaps and a service visit runs you, then compare. For a lot of homes it comes out even or ahead, and you stop having to think about any of it.
If the math does not work for your setup, no problem at all. Reply and I will tell you straight.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
**Send timing:** Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET.
**Expected performance:**
- Open: 40-46% (list-wide avg is 42.3%; this is a warm, named, relevant segment, so I expect at or slightly above avg. The recent 0.2-0.4% campaigns are junk-subject outliers I'm discounting.)
- Click: 3-6% (well above the 0.23% avg because there is a real reason to reply and the CTA is a low-friction reply, not an app login)
- Conversion: 4-8 net new Concierge sign-ups (5-8% of engaged openers). At $99/mo that is ~$4,700-$9,500/yr recurring.
**Source justification:** Draws from CONCIERGE UPSELL CONTEXT (the "year 1.5 is it worth it, here's the math" framing and $99 feature list, explicitly permitted for the pre-filtered 13-24 month list) and JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS (concierge upsell candidates). Compliant with Hard Rule 1 (all recipients past 12 months). Legacy name "Re-Ionator Pro and WT RO" suppressed per Hard Rule 2, replaced with tenure line.
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 day satisfied clients)
items.preview:
**Audience:** Referral push candidates, 30 members (30-60 days post-install, satisfied).
**Why this one:** These clients are in the honeymoon window. Newly installed, water noticeably better, not yet eligible for Concierge or annual service. The only correct ask right now is referrals, and the bonus structure is a strong, concrete hook. Note: Janine Stenson's system is "ClearWave Sovereign," a **current** brand name, so I can name it. The rest get the tenure line.
**Subject line (primary):**
`Know someone drinking bad water? Read this`
**Alternates:**
1. (specific) `$500 when your referral becomes a client`
2. (curiosity) `A quick thank you (and an offer)`
3. (authority) `The reason most of our clients find us`
4. (pain) `Your neighbors probably have the water you had`
**Preview text:**
`If you know someone who could use better water, here is how we say thank you.`
**Body (Sovereign owner version, e.g. Janine):**
Hi Janine,
You have had your ClearWave Sovereign for about a month now, so the difference in your water has probably stopped being a novelty and started being just... normal. That is the goal.
Here is the thing: most of the people we help came from a client like you telling a friend. So if someone you know is dealing with the water you used to have, here is how we say thank you.
Refer someone and when they become a client, you get $500 cash. Refer more over the year and it climbs to $750, then $1,000. Even if they just book a consult and do not move forward, we send you a $50 gift card for the introduction.
They get a free water assessment. You get taken care of. Simple.
Just reply with a name or have them mention you when they call.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
**Body (non-current-name version, e.g. Regina):** identical, except open with:
> It has been about a month since we installed your water system, so the difference in your water has probably stopped being a novelty and started being just... normal.
**Send timing:** Thursday, 11:00 AM ET.
**Expected performance:**
- Open: 42-48% (recent, happy, named clients; slightly above list avg)
- Click/reply: 2-4% (concrete cash figure drives replies; lower than Concierge because the ask requires them to have a person in mind)
- Conversion: 2-4 referred consults, 1-2 likely to close over the following weeks. Even one closed referral funds itself many times over.
**Source justification:** Draws from REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE (exact $500/$750/$1,000 and $50 gift card figures) and JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS (referral push candidates, 30-60 days). Complies with Hard Rule 3 (referrals, never reviews), Hard Rule 3a ("free water assessment" used exactly), and Hard Rule 2 (Sovereign named because current; legacy names suppressed via tenure line).
---
**One flag for you, Justin:** I deliberately did **not** propose the 1,000-person cold re-engagement blast this week. Your Mailchimp health shows recent campaigns crashing to 0.2-0.4% opens, which suggests deliverability/reputation damage. Blasting 1,000 disengaged contacts now risks further spam-flagging and could drag down the warm campaigns above. If you want the cold segment worked, I'd recommend a small (100-200) throttled test with a genuine water-news hook first, sent after these two warm sends land. Say the word and I'll draft it.

---
